blocking.issue: The CI parity guarantee still claims more than the pipeline delivers. It says a Bundle that passes `ruralz bundle validate` also passes Ruralz Control ingest and Node activation with identical diagnostics. The same section adds checks after the digest that `validate` never runs: the online Plugin check (RZ-CFG-028) runs at `build`, at ingest and at activation, secret resolution (RZ-CFG-026) runs only on Nodes, and the schema-level skew check (RZ-CFG-024) runs at Rollout. The document also never says whether `validate` runs the online stage at all. An operator who uses `validate` as the merge gate will expect green CI to mean the Revision activates, and it may not.
blocking.evidence: Line 768: "a Bundle that passes `ruralz bundle validate` in CI passes Ruralz Control ingest (Git or CRD) and Node activation with identical diagnostics." Line 800: "`ruralz bundle build` runs it unless `--offline` is set, Ruralz Control runs it at ingest, and Nodes run it at activation, where a failure is a NACK. Every failure is RZ-CFG-028." Line 743: "An unresolvable reference is RZ-CFG-026: the Node rejects the Revision (a NACK in Control mode)". Line 956: "Ruralz Control refuses to start a Rollout ... (RZ-CFG-024)".
blocking.fix: Limit the guarantee to the offline stages: "passes the offline stages of Ruralz Control ingest and Node activation with identical diagnostics". Add one sentence listing what can still fail after a green `validate`: RZ-CFG-028 (online Plugin check), RZ-CFG-024 (Node schema level), RZ-CFG-026 (secret resolution on the Node) and RZ-CFG-027 (digest mismatch on push). State whether `validate` runs the online stage. For example, say it is offline by default and add an `--online` flag, recorded in OQ-configuration-model-10, or tell operators to gate on `ruralz bundle build`.

blocking.section: Bundle layout and merge / Overlays; Secrets and environment variables / Environment substitution
blocking.issue: Overlays, `--env` and `--environments` have no milestone tag, and their dependencies make the M1 story contradictory. The Summary says every capability carries a milestone tag. The `validate`, `render`, `diff` and `build` verbs are `Planned (M1)`. But with `--env`, the CLI reads variables only from `Environment` resources, either from a file or from Ruralz Control. The `Environment` kind is control-plane-only and `Planned (M2)`, and Ruralz Control arrives in M2. Without `--env`, a render applies "no overlay". So at M1 an operator cannot tell whether `overlays/<env>/` exists, or whether the CLI parses `Environment` files before the kind ships.
blocking.evidence: Line 17: "Nothing is implemented yet; every capability carries a milestone tag." Line 33: "The `ruralz bundle` verbs `validate`, `render`, `diff` and `build` are `Planned (M1)`". Line 105: "| `Environment`, `Cluster` | Control plane only, outside the Bundle | Planned (M2) |". Line 757: "That Environment's `spec.variables`, read from the file named by `--environments` or fetched from Ruralz Control; never the process environment; with neither source, an error". Line 758: "The same verbs without `--env` | CLI process environment, for local development; no overlay". No `Planned (Mx)` tag appears in Overlays (lines 579-596).
blocking.fix: Add explicit tags. For example, give overlays and `--env`/`--environments` their own milestone, and state which of these holds: (a) the CLI reads `Environment` files from M1, so the Environment file format is `Planned (M1)` and only its Ruralz Control ingestion is `Planned (M2)`; or (b) overlays are `Planned (M2)`, and in M1 local renders use the process environment with no overlay. Update the Scope of kinds table and the renderer table to match. Also tag the other untagged capabilities in this document: the restricted YAML profile, the canonical form and Revision digest, `render --effective`, diff against `/config/dump` (Drift) and version skew, or narrow the Summary claim.
